```plato
//==
// # Polyhedra
//
// Sections, in order:
//  - Named solids as Conway programs on the seeds
//  - The remaining nine Catalan duals
//  - The expand, bevel and snub Archimedeans
//  - Dual, ambo and truncate on polygon meshes
//  - Expand, snub and bevel on polygon meshes
//  - Kis, join and needle on polygon meshes
//  - Ortho, meta and gyro on polygon meshes
//  - Chamfer, propeller, zip and reflect on polygon meshes
//  - Reading a polyhedron
//  - Polyhedral dual pairings on the solid kinds
//  - The five Platonic solids as polygon meshes

library Polyhedra
{
    //==
    // # Named solids as Conway programs on the seeds
    //
    // The Archimedean and Catalan solids this tree can name so far, each a one-line
    // Conway program over a Platonic seed
    // rather than another coordinate table. Read
    // as `PolygonMesh3D.Cuboctahedron`, `PolygonMesh3D.RhombicDodecahedron`, …
    //
    // This covers the ambo and truncate families and their duals. The expand,
    // bevel and snub families, and the remaining nine Catalan duals, follow in the
    // next two sections; together the three catalogs name all thirteen of each of
    // the `ArchimedeanSolid` / `CatalanSolid` sums in `solids.types.plato`.
    //
    // Vertices are NOT normalized to a common radius: the Archimedeans below are
    // vertex-transitive and may be passed through ProjectedToUnitSphere, the
    // Catalans must not be.

    //==
    // Archimedean — rectified seeds (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archimedean_solid).

    // 8 triangles + 6 squares on 12 vertices
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuboctahedron).
    Cuboctahedron(_: PolygonMesh3D): PolygonMesh3D
        => PolygonMesh3D.Cube.Ambo;
```
